key_insight: Protein Autoregressive Modeling (PAR) generates protein backbones by sculpting structures in a coarse-to-fine, multiscale autoregressive fashion—predicting finer-scale geometry conditioned on coarser topology to capture hierarchical protein structure efficiently.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of generating realistic protein backbone structures that require modeling long-range and hierarchical dependencies across multiple spatial scales, which single-scale generative methods struggle to capture.
method: Multi-scale downsampling to represent backbone geometry at multiple resolutions (coarse → fine).
Autoregressive next-scale prediction: at each scale, generate finer-scale coordinates conditioned on the current coarser representation.
Iterative coarse-to-fine refinement with structure-aware objectives to preserve topology while adding geometric detail.
impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable framework for protein structure generation that better models hierarchical geometry, enabling more realistic backbone sampling and easier integration into protein design and generative ML workflows.
visual_elements: Sculpting analogy diagram: a statue progressing from blocky coarse form to detailed final structure (coarse→fine stages).
Pipeline flowchart: multi-scale downsampling → autoregressive next-scale generator → refinement loop.
Sequence of snapshots showing the same protein backbone at 3–4 scales to illustrate added detail per step.
Schematic comparing single-scale vs. multiscale generation to highlight improved hierarchical modeling (icon or bar/arrow graphic).
paper_title: Protein Autoregressive Modeling via Multiscale Structure Generation
paper_authors: Yanru Qu, Cheng-Yen Hsieh, Zaixiang Zheng, Ge Liu, Quanquan Gu
